summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Hydra Tech through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for latency-sensitive chat features and wants a 2-week pilot with benchmarks and SOC2 + network diagram before procurement.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya from our SE team is here to run the console walkthrough. 
[00:09] Martin Lopez: Morning. We got about 40 minutes, excited to see the analytics and costs. We want to understand run-rate and what breaks if we go Dedicated.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Great, I'll share my screen - starting with the usage analytics. This is per-route breakdown, tokens, latencies, and cost per thousand tokens. You can filter by model, route, and time window.
[00:28] Elena Novak: Quick Q - do those costs include batching and cache savings? Sometimes our numbers look off when batching kicks in.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Good question. The console shows raw token cost plus an adjusted view that factors in batching and prefix/KV cache savings. We infer effective per-token cost based on observed batching efficiency and cache hit rate.
[00:47] [00:47] Jasmine Park: Is that automatic or we need to enable it?
[00:50] Priya Nair: It's on by default for hosted; for Dedicated we surface suggestions in Optimize tab - e.g., tweak batch size, enable KV cache and quantization profile to reduce cost.
[01:02] Alex Chen: To set context, Hydra said you have a latency SLO of 250ms p95 for chat and want to keep inference cost under a target. Can you confirm?
[01:10] Martin Lopez: Yep. 250ms p95 for user-facing chat; background async workloads can be slower. Our budget target is roughly $0.02 per 1k tokens across average traffic, but we can be flexible if latency improves.
[01:22] Priya Nair: Ok makes sense. On this customer route view you can pin targets and get alerts when cost or latency drifts - we also do regression alerts tied to eval sets.
[01:33] [01:33] Raj Patel: Security question - where do logs live? We need audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:38] Alex Chen: We support audit logs to your SIEM, optional private deployments with a customer-managed control plane, and KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share SOC2 + network diagram after the call.
[01:47] Priya Nair: Back to dashboards - here's a per-route flame graph showing latency contributors: tokenization, model compute, and network. You can click into traces and see per-request payloads (redacted), model version, and kernel profile.
[02:05] [02:05] Martin Lopez: Nice - can we group routes by user journey? Our chat flows have multiple calls per interaction.
[02:10] Priya Nair: Yes, you can tag routes and roll up metrics. The cost breakdown page will roll up by tag or service.
[02:18] Alex Chen: Let me show the cost breakdown sheet - per-model, per-route, and predicted monthly spend based on current traffic.
[02:25] Priya Nair: For example, route "user_chat_v2" is using a 13B open model with quantization q4 and we show effective cost of $0.035 per 1k tokens, but if you switch to a smaller tuned model or enable more aggressive batching you can hit $0.01-$0.02.
[02:40] [02:40] Jasmine Park: Those model names sometimes get munged in our logs, do you map model aliases?
[02:44] Priya Nair: We do alias mapping and version pins. Also automatic fallback rules - if a model variant is incompatible we route to a compatible variant preserving API.
[02:55] Alex Chen: On Dedicated, you'd get better tail latency predictability - fewer noisy neighbors - but with more fixed cost. We'll show an ROI calc for your traffic pattern.
[03:06] Martin Lopez: That's the tradeoff we expected. Do you offer burst capacity if we get spikes?
[03:10] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated has configurable burst policies and autoscaling; Hosted uses multi-tenant pools with fallbacks.
[03:18] [03:18] Elena Novak: For the pilot we want a 2-week benchmark, can you simulate our traffic and reproduce latency and cost numbers?
[03:25] Priya Nair: Absolutely - we'll ingest sample traffic patterns and run a pilot in Dedicated-like environment. We'll capture per-route dashboards, KV cache hit rates, batching stats, and cost.
[03:35] Alex Chen: I'll put that in next steps. Also Hydra asked about eval/regression monitoring?
[03:40] Priya Nair: We tie quality monitors to prompt/eval sets. If responses degrade you can trigger alerts or automatic rollback to a previous model.
[03:48] [03:48] Raj Patel: Does the private deployment option allow air-gapped? We have one regulated product that may require on-prem.
[03:53] Alex Chen: Yes - Private supports on-prem or VPC control plane; we can discuss the packaging and support contract separately.
[04:00] Priya Nair: Showing the Optimize tab now - suggestions for batching, quantization, and model swaps. For your heavy chat route, enable prefix caching for repeat conversational user data to cut token re-compute.
[04:12] [04:12] Jasmine Park: Any gotchas with prefix caching on PII data?
[04:15] Priya Nair: You can configure cache policies and TTLs; with Private you can enforce customer-side encryption for cached state. We'll work with Security to ensure compliance.
[04:25] Alex Chen: I'll ask Priya to include the cache recommendations in the pilot plan.
[04:30] Priya Nair: Switching back to the per-route cost table - you can export CSV and break down by time window; also we have a 'what-if' planner to estimate cost if you change model or batching.
[04:42] [04:42] Martin Lopez: Can we get a sample export of our projected monthly cost for 1M monthly users?
[04:48] Priya Nair: Yes, send the traffic pattern and we'll run those numbers. For 1M users, depending on tokens per session and caching, you could see large variance; that's why we suggest a short pilot.
[05:00] Alex Chen: Ok, quick product/technical deep-dive: Priya, can you talk about kernel selection and quantization impact on latency?
[05:06] Priya Nair: Sure - runtime selects kernels based on model architecture and sequence length distribution. Quantized kernels reduce memory bandwidth and can lower cost but may change latency profile. We profile per-model and surface recommended quantization profiles.
[05:20] [05:20] Raj Patel: Regulatory - do you provide audit logs for model decisions and tracing for data lineage?
[05:26] Priya Nair: Yes, request/response traces, model versioning, and rollout records are logged. For Private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM or provide log retention options.
[05:36] [05:36] Jasmine Park: What about RBAC and SSO?
[05:40] Alex Chen: SSO via SAML/OIDC supported; role-based access controls in Console; we'll include admin role examples in the docs.
[05:47] Priya Nair: If there's time I'll demo the route-level trace drilldown - it shows the KV cache hit, batching window size, and GPU utilization per request.
[05:57] [06:00] Priya Nair: (demoing) here's a trace where we can see caching saved ~30% of tokens and batching reduced latency at 95th for that minute.
[06:12] Martin Lopez: That's helpful. Any limitations on model types? We use some custom Llama variants internally.
[06:18] Priya Nair: We support a wide catalog including Llama-family variants; some custom forks may need conversion steps for runtime compatibility - our onboarding team handles model compilation and kernel tuning.
[06:30] [06:30] Elena Novak: About billing - how granular is the cost attribution? We need project-level billing for our finance team.
[06:36] Alex Chen: Per-route and per-team billing is supported; you can tag routes to projects and get per-project invoices.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Also graph of cost over time and alerts when projected monthly spend exceeds thresholds.
[06:50] [06:50] Martin Lopez: Ok, next practical steps - we want pricing, SOC2, network diagram, and a pilot plan.
[06:56] Alex Chen: Action items - we'll send those. Any final concerns?
[07:02] Jasmine Park: Would like to see network egress estimates for Dedicated.
[07:06] Priya Nair: We'll include egress calc in the proposal.
[07:10] [07:10] Alex Chen: Great. Recap: Alex to send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram; Priya to prepare benchmark/pilot plan and run the what-if cost scenarios; Hydra to share traffic pattern and SLOs. We'll schedule the infra deep-dive next week.
[07:28] Martin Lopez: Sounds good, thanks.
[07:31] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:34] [END TRANSCRIPT]
notes: Customer leaning Dedicated for latency predictability but wants Hosted cost comparison
Pilot requested: 2-week benchmark with real traffic
Security needs: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, network diagram
